jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11490_34_FR_17567...txt and jobs/family-rule-tail/output/texts/EO_11490_tail.txt (FR print lists EO 11094 of February 26, 1963)
reasoning: I compared the genuine claim field by field with the planted version I reviewed blind. The only differences are the 16 first_end dates and the whole_order_end date, which now read 1969-10-28 and, for the Sec. 14 revocation sentence, 1963-02-26. Those dates match EO 11490 (signed October 28, 1969; Sec. 3015 item (21) revokes 'Executive Order No. 11094 of February 26, 1963') and EO 11094's own signature date, and they agree with the claim's prose. No mechanical receipt was supplied, so I checked hashes and quotes myself: all 35 quoted source references have matching text_sha256 values and exact quotes at their offsets, and every scope's text equals the held bytes. The working-text confirmation record has no offsets; its hashes match the EO 11490 APP text and the page record. Identity: number, date and title agree with the census register. The inventory is complete: the lead, Secs. 1-13, and Sec. 14 split into precedence and the revocation of EP Order No. 10 and DMOs 1-20, 1-22 and 1-24 (that revocation was executed on issuance). The paraphrases of Secs. 2-10 match the text, and the claim's statement that EO 10952 is cited in Sec. 9 (Cooperation with Department of Defense) is correct. The cruden search found no earlier end; the only hits are EO 11490 copies. Savings: Sec. 3014 yields to Sec. 3015, and the claim honestly bounds what it did not read. Raw originals are uncommitted (a custody gap, not a ground for rejection).
